tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Identify the largest disk that is not yet on its goal peg. First clear any smaller disks that block it, then move that disk directly to its goal peg. This reduces the problem size by one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest remaining disk is not on its target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk while smaller disks remain on top of it, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To relocate a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg using the third peg as auxiliary, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the largest of the k disks to the target, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to move a contiguous stack of disks from one peg to another.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk without first moving the smaller disks that sit above it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response must end with a syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier extracts the last parseable list. Any preceding text is ignored.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Embedding the moves inside a sentence or omitting a closing bracket, so the parser cannot extract a complete list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Replay each move mentally (or on paper) from the given initial state and check that after the last move the pegs match the goal configuration exactly.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After generating the move list, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg or in the wrong order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer should consist solely of the move list; any surrounding commentary, headings, or formatting will be ignored or cause parsing errors.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory sentences before the list, causing the parser to stop at the first non‑list token.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, confirm that the source peg’s top disk matches the disk being moved and that the destination peg is empty or has a larger top disk. This prevents illegal placements.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During move generation, for every candidate move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere. This maintains the size ordering invariant.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately before moving a larger disk onto a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk5 onto peg2 while disk2 is already on peg2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto a peg if a larger disk will later need to be placed there, unless you plan to move the small disk away before the larger one arrives. This prevents blocking the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When considering moving a small disk onto a peg that is intended for a larger disk later.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing the smallest disk onto the final target peg and never moving it away before moving larger disks onto that peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, first relocate all smaller disks that sit above it to other pegs, respecting the size rules. This frees the larger disk for movement.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk4 while disk3 remains on top of it on the same peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Smallest-disk cyclic move strategy
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Repeatedly move the smallest disk to the next peg in a fixed cyclic order (e.g., 0→1→2→0) and then make the only other legal move that does not involve the smallest disk. This alternating pattern guarantees progress and avoids dead ends, especially when the initial configuration is arbitrary.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing a move sequence, use this alternating pattern to systematically relocate disks while respecting all constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Stalling the solution by moving larger disks while the smallest disk stays on a peg that blocks the needed move, resulting in no legal move for the larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to output any moves, often after focusing on reasoning or due to truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always conclude the response with a complete, syntactically correct list of moves, even if the puzzle is already solved.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generating before finishing the list, possibly due to token limits or early termination.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the list ends with a closing bracket and includes all intended moves; count moves if needed.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk without checking the current top of the source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before adding a move, verify that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model places a small disk on the goal peg before larger disks have been moved there, blocking them.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: If a small disk is placed on the final target peg, ensure it is moved away before any larger disk needs that peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not check the size ordering of the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the disk being moved.
